objectives_source: Neither the page frontmatter nor tasks/docs/artifacts/T5.research.json records objectives; the research artifact carries objectives: [] because it ran in affected mode, where the contract leaves that field empty. The six below are derived from what the page plainly sets out to teach, so the gap analysis still happens. They are proposals, not a record, and the orchestrator should either adopt them or replace them.

objective_gaps.objective: explain what a persona is made of
objective_gaps.why: The six parts are a term list under §What a persona is made of, each with a one-line definition, and the non-verbal tags follow it. No gap.

objective_gaps.objective: describe how your first persona is made
objective_gaps.why: §Making your first one covers the interview, the scripted opening and farewell, the handover, and the second-brain beat, and links onward to The second brain. No gap.

objective_gaps.objective: describe how to make a persona after first run has ended
objective_gaps.why: This is the reader dead end the corpus pass is named after, and §Making another one closes it: first run expires the moment the first persona is written, so you ask the persona you have, who is born holding create_persona; the grant is one tool wide; nothing needs restarting; and the house does not switch, so you switch by name. The pre-2026-09-03 caveat names two routes for a reader the grant never reached. The action is conversational rather than a UI path, so a concept page can carry it whole without becoming a procedure.

The two concept pages now disagree, and T27 owns closing that.

objective_gaps.objective: describe what you can change about a persona later, and what you cannot
objective_gaps.why: Partially taught. The page states what the Personas page edits, that saving restarts the house while making a persona does not, that removal sits behind developer mode, and that a removal renames rather than deletes. Two holes remain. The route to the removal control is written nowhere in the corpus, because the concept page correctly refuses the procedure and the how-to it should link to does not exist (F1, T32). And the precondition on removing the default persona, 'until you have set another', names an action no client appears to expose (F4).

objective_gaps.objective: change or remove a persona on the Personas page
objective_gaps.why: An apply-level objective the page raises and cannot serve. Under the Bloom mapping, apply implies a how-to, and wiki/page-types.md:153-154 forbids the steps here. This is not a wrong-type finding against this page: the level belongs to a sibling page that does not exist. desktop-client/src/components/personas/PersonasView.tsx:28 names wiki/clients/persona-page.md as its design of record and the file is absent. Until T32 lands, this objective is taught by no page in the corpus.

Every section maps to one of the six objectives above: the six parts, first run, making another, on-disk layout, voice, switching and pinning, and changing later. §Voices, briefly is the only candidate for belonging elsewhere, and it earns its place because a designed voice is one of the six parts, it summarises rather than duplicates, and it hands off to Voice and the voice engine at the end.

detailed_review.score_reasoning:
Baseline 10 - (F1 2 + F2 1 + F3 0.5 + F4 1 + F5 1 + F6 0.5 + F7 0.5) = 3.5, floored to 3. After the checklist, open penalty is F1 2 + F4 1 = 3, so 10 - 3 = 7. Delta +4. Read the 3 carefully before acting on it: it is not a verdict on the prose, which is among the best in this corpus, and the author's five corrections all hold up against source. Two thirds of the baseline penalty sat in things whose fix is not on this page at all, F1 at 2 and F4 at 1, and both are still open, which is the whole reason the page cannot pass. The 7 is therefore an accurate reading of the page a reader meets today: it teaches everything it sets out to teach except how to act on the surface it spends three sections describing.

The colour/color conflict, adjudicated. The author's reading of the linter is right in effect and slightly wrong in detail, and the detail matters. scripts/lint_wiki.py:339-340 runs the BRITISH pattern (line 97, which includes colour\w*) over every body line outside a fenced block and appends a Finding at the default severity, error (line 137). There is no exemption at that call site for any page. QUOTES_BANNED_FORMS (line 120) is consulted only at line 341 for terminology and line 375 for reader-drift, so it is not that the quote exemption is reserved for the style guide: british-spelling has no quote exemption anywhere, and style-guide.md passes only because line 170 happens to list the American forms. So the conclusion stands. Quoting the shipped sentence whole in prose would take the corpus off zero errors and fail the build.

Two mechanical escapes exist and both should be refused. strip_code at line 253 removes inline code spans before the check, so `colour` in backticks would pass, and body_lines at 203-205 skips fenced blocks entirely. Setting a spoken word in code voice tells the reader it is an identifier, and putting product dialogue in a fenced block renders it as terminal output. Neither is worth smuggling one word past a rule.

Which resolution is right: change the product string. OPENING_TEXT at backend/harness/valar/gateway/first_run.py:47-53 is user-facing product copy, spoken on every install, in a product whose own documentation standard is American spelling (wiki/style-guide.md:168-171). One word in one string is the cheapest fix available and the only one that leaves the wiki free to quote the sentence whole and accurately. The alternative, teaching the linter to exempt quoted material, is worse than the problem: it would need a general 'inside double quotes' carve-out that punches a hole in every prose rule the linter enforces, and the product would still be spelling against its own documentation. Scope note: colour is also the required parameter name in tools.yaml:1093-1127 and in creation.py, those are identifiers, they appear in docs in code voice, and strip_code already exempts them. I am not recommending they change. The recommendation is the one spoken string.

Until that lands, the author's truncation is the correct interim and I kept it. What I fixed was the framing around it (F6): the page claimed the quote was the opening line and it is two sentences of a longer one.

On the three orchestrator rulings, all three are right and I would not reverse any. Keeping the two developer-mode switches off a concept page follows wiki/page-types.md:153-154 exactly. The pre-2026-09-03 caveat is load-bearing, because the grant reached only persona_template.json and nothing migrates an existing manifest, so without it the page's central new fact is false for every house that predates the change. And refusing to document the T31 handover defect is right for the stated reason. Note that refusing to document the defect is not the same as leaving the reader with the wrong model, which is what F2 fixed: the page now states the intended behaviour, that the house does not switch outside first run, without mentioning the announcement that misleads. If the orchestrator reads that sentence as too close to the ruling, it is one sentence in §Making another one and is cleanly reversible.
detailed_review.what_worked:
F2 is the one that matters for the journey this pass is named after. §Making another one closed the 'how do I create a persona after first run' dead end, but it stopped at 'the folder is written' and left the reader holding an expectation the previous section had set: in first run, the new persona takes the house and greets you first. A reader who makes a second persona and hears nothing had no way to tell success from failure. The section now ends by telling them who they are talking to and how to reach the person they just made.

F3 repaired a forward reference that hit exactly the wrong reader. 'The Personas page' was first used inside the Note written for someone whose house predates the grant, 54 lines before the page says what that surface is, and that reader is the one most in need of a route. It is now glossed and linked at first mention.

F5 put a figure request against the one surface the corpus never shows anyone. F6 stopped the page overstating a quotation, on the very sentence whose accuracy this run was asked to adjudicate. F7 removed a genuine ambiguity rather than a cosmetic one: 'the phone' is the standing term for the Android device elsewhere in the corpus, so 'The phone and Android write far less' was unreadable for an Android reader.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down:
F1, worth 2, is the whole gap between this page and a pass. The page invites the reader to change a persona, re-grant its tools, replace its voice clip and remove it, and there is no page in the corpus that tells them how to do any of it. Removal is the sharpest case: it sits behind two switches, the concept page correctly refuses to name them, and no other page names them either, so the route exists in the product and nowhere in the documentation. The destination is already named in the source, at desktop-client/src/components/personas/PersonasView.tsx:28, as wiki/clients/persona-page.md, and that file does not exist. This is T32.

F4, worth 1, is a sentence that tells a reader to do something first and may point at nothing. Removing the default persona requires setting another, and the default comes only from HEARTH_DEFAULT_PERSONA in hearth.env at install. The risk is sharpened by the page itself: two sections earlier it describes the per-device 'Start with' pin, which a reader will reasonably mistake for the default.

One thing visible on regrade that did not meet the detraction floor and is recorded rather than scored: the Note in §Making another one opens 'A persona made before 2026-09-03 does not carry this grant. It reached the template...', where 'It' means the grant but sits next to 'a persona' as the nearer noun.

On three pages deliberately untouched: wiki/backend/tool-catalog.md still states this page's central new fact is impossible (T26), wiki/features/voice.md still carries two of the four claims corrected here (T27), and wiki/first-run.md still treats the no-restart behaviour as unsolved (T28). None were edited and none are scored against this page, but until they land the corpus contradicts itself on the one fact T5 exists to establish.
